subject: BrightRetail: hosted API baseline + vendor comparison and rate request
messages:
From: BrightRetail Procurement <procurement@brightretail.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: hosted API baseline + competitor pricing (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS)

Hi Aisha,

We're evaluating hosted LLM options for BrightRetail's search-and-personalization stack and need a clear baseline rate card to compare unit economics across vendors. Specifically we want:
- Per-1K token pricing for standard generation (short form, avg 150 tokens) and long-form (avg 1,200 tokens)
- Embedding pricing per 1K vectors and any volume tiers
- Notes on burst/scale penalties and SLA implications
- Any standard discounts for committed monthly spend (we expect ~120M tokens/month initially)

Also, could you include a short comparison showing how Redwood's effective price at our profile stacks up vs OpenAI, Anthropic, Together, and AWS (ballpark numbers are fine if you can’t share exact list prices)? We want to run a TCO exercise this week.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30m today or tomorrow.

— Elena Ramos
Procurement Manager, BrightRetail Inc
[Attachment: brightretail_usage_profile.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)]

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ramos <procurement@brightretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: hosted API baseline + competitor pricing (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS)

Elena —

Thanks for the note and the usage profile — got it. We can pull together a tailored baseline and a competitor comparison. Quick clarifying questions so the numbers we send are comparable:

1) Are the 120M tokens/month expected to be steady-state, or front-loaded with a ramp (if ramp, what's month 1 vs month 6)?
2) What embedding size do you use (512 vs 768 vs custom) and approximate queries/day?
3) Is latency SLO strict (p95 < 150ms) or can you tolerate higher p95 if it reduces cost?

I'll assemble a draft ratecard and a short competitor table. Do you prefer a PDF summary + spreadsheet? I can include an optional committed-usage discount schedule and a canary/fallback plan that uses cheaper model variants during peak.

Proposed next step: 30m review on Thu 8/14 10:00am PT — does that work?

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_ratecard_q3_draft.pdf (PDF, 72KB)]

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-12T11:09:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightRetail request — need competitive comp + recommended offer

Marissa / Vivek — forwarding BrightRetail's ask (below). They want a baseline hosted API rate + competitor comparison against OpenAI / Anthropic / Together / AWS.

Key constraints: 120M tokens/month steady-state likely, latency preference TBD (I asked). They also want embedding pricing and note on burst/scale.

What I'm thinking:
- Base hosted list: $0.025 per 1K input tokens / $0.05 per 1K output tokens (example baseline)
- Embeddings: $0.45 per 1K vectors (512-d) with volume tiers at 10M / 50M / 200M
- Committed discount bands: 10% @ $10k/mo, 20% @ $25k/mo, 30% @ $60k/mo (we should make these discretionary; recommend quoting a starting committed ask to lock 20% first)
- Competitive notes to include (ballpark): OpenAI often quoted in public channels at ~$0.03/$0.06 for similar models; Anthropic typically slightly lower on some pricing lists for higher-context models; Together and AWS have varied pricing by model/marketplace — AWS often includes infra+license that can appear similar but has different burst constraints.

Marissa — can you draft a 1-page competitor table with suggested Redwood effective price at 120M tokens (showing with/without 20% commit)? Vivek — can you confirm whether we should include an explicit burst policy (e.g., short-term +50% burst at same unit price up to 48 hours) or offer a throttled fallback to cheaper variants?

Thanks — I want to send BrightRetail a neat PDF + spreadsheet by EOD Wed.

Aisha

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-13T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightRetail request — need competitive comp + recommended offer

Aisha —

Attached is the draft competitive table and two price scenarios (conservative/accelerator). High level notes in the table:
- OpenAI: public-ish ranges we see are ~ $0.03 prompt / $0.06 completion for mid-capacity models; variable with context window. Effective blended (120M tokens, mix 150/1,200) puts them at approx $3.6k–$4.8k/day gross.
- Anthropic: slightly lower in a few negotiated deals; for our comparatives use ~10–15% lower than OpenAI on equivalent throughput.
- Together: competitive on committed deals but fewer regions; discount flexibility high when customers commit to associated infra.
- AWS Marketplace: appears higher on list price but includes marketplace fees; effective cost can be similar once you include reserved instances for Dedicated.

Proposed Redwood offer (two scenarios):
- Conservative: $0.022 / 1K input + $0.048 / 1K output, embeddings $0.42 / 1K vectors, 15% discount @ $15k/mo commit.
- Accelerator (preferred): $0.018 / 1K input + $0.04 / 1K output, embeddings $0.36 / 1K vectors, 25% discount @ $40k/mo commit + 2-month onboarding credit.

I'll attach the spreadsheet with the TCO calc. Recommend we lead with the Accelerator in the call and be ready to fall back to Conservative in writing.

[Attachment: competitive_pricing_table.xlsx (XLSX, 96KB)]

— Marissa

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ramos <procurement@brightretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-19T16:07:00-07:00
Subject: BrightRetail: Redwood hosted API offer + comparison (attached)

Elena —

Thanks for the conversation last week. Attached is a short PDF summary and a spreadsheet that shows a direct TCO at your 120M tokens/month profile with two tiered offers. Summary below: 

1) Accelerator Offer (recommended):
   - Generation: $0.018 per 1K input tokens / $0.040 per 1K output tokens
   - Embeddings: $0.36 per 1K vectors (512-d)
   - Commit: 25% discount with $40k/month minimum for 12 months
   - Value adds: 2 months onboarding credit, first 30 days of traffic warm-cache waived, one free canary rollout (technical support)

2) Conservative Offer:
   - Generation: $0.022 per 1K input / $0.048 per 1K output
   - Embeddings: $0.42 per 1K vectors
   - Commit: 15% discount with $15k/month minimum for 12 months

Competitive comparison (ballpark):
- OpenAI: public indications put a similar profile ~10–35% more expensive than our Accelerator scenario at list prices, depending on model and context length.
- Anthropic: can be competitive on a per-model basis; we expect them ~5–15% cheaper than OpenAI in many negotiated cases but often with more limited region coverage.
- Together: can match effective cost if they package infra — watch for regional availability and support SLAs.
- AWS: often similar or slightly higher once marketplace fees and reserved infra are included; advantage is integration with AWS infra.

Attachments: redwood_ratecard_q3_draft.pdf, brightretail_tco_120M_tokens.xlsx

Would you like us to convert the Accelerator offer into a formal SOW and draft contract? We can also run a short 2-week proof-of-concept at a 50% credit to validate latency and cost assumptions.

If Thu 8/21 11am PT works, I’ll schedule a 30m to walk through the spreadsheet and next steps.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
